newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Everbright units in buying spree - brokers.
newsitem.headline: China Everbright units in buying spree - brokers.

text.p: The Hong Kong-listed units of Beijing-based China Everbright Group Ltd appear to be launching a major fundraising exercise to chase strategic acquisitions, brokers said on Tuesday.
Trading in shares of China Everbright-IHD Pacific Ltd, China Everbright Technology Ltd and China Everbright International Ltd has been suspended pending announcements.
"They are definitely on the acquisition trail," said Lino Delgado, associate director at Amsteel Securities.
Senior Everbright executives contacted on Tuesday would not comment on the suspensions.
"It's placements, and it is likely that involves all three companies," a broker with a large regional house said.
A flurry of rumours on fundraising efforts and other market talk linking the group to several listed companies circulated on Tuesday.

According to that talk, the group is embarking on a series of acquisitions which involve the entire group and follow its parent company's surprise acquisition of a 7.74 percent stake in Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd for HK$11.4 billion.
The parent company is also believed to be seeking funds in the debt market since it will need to make payment on its Hongkong Telecom purchase by June 3.
Most of the market talk focused on Everbright-IHD.
Local newspapers reported the company was planning a placement of new and old new shares to raise HK$1.88 billion.
The reports on Tuesday said the parent company placed 87 million old shares at HK$10.75 to institutions then took an issue of 175 million new shares at HK$10.75.

The funds were likely to be used to acquire a 20 percent stake in Everbright Bank of China, which is the only joint stock bank in China and is 51 percent held by the China Everbright Group, analysts said.
The stake in Everbright Bank is estimated to cost between HK$1.2 billion and HK$1.6 billion, they said.
Everbright-IHD has also been rumoured to be interested in taking a stake in Theme International. Theme shares were suspended on Monday pending an announcement.
China Everbright Technology Ltd has been linked with several manufacturers of electronics and telecommunications products.
"Market talk says the company is looking to buy into another technology company, possibly Contrad International," said the head of research at a local brokerage.
China Everbright Group set up its "technology" arm by taking over the listing of Hanwah Holdings Ltd in January 1994. Hanwah made audio products, television sets and cassette players.
But Everbright Technology has never looked well focused, analysts said.

In December 1996, the company said it had completed a restructuring of its assets, including the disposal of 14 subsidiaries and three associate companies involved in television and consumer audio products manufacturing.
At the end of 1996, management said the company was seeking investments in information technology in China.
China Everbright International, which was suspended on Tuesday, has also undergone some restructuring in recent months.
In January, the company said it would acquire a majority stake in Shenzhen Everbright Timber Industry Co Ltd for HK$449.52 million.
In April, the company announced the disposal of its Hong Kong-based financial services business to its Beijing-based parent for HK$25.6 million.
